_comment: Ten silent recordings of buying eight books for Threads commenters, cut into one film. There is no speech anywhere -- the Windows window-capture wrote a digitally silent track (-91 dB) -- so the cut is driven by screen activity, not by pauses. Voice-over is added in a later pass, which is why the render carries no audio stream at all.

regions._comment: x=0.748 is the Edge side-panel divider, measured off frames from every recording rather than assumed. 'main' is the browser doing the work; 'panel' is Claude thinking out loud, which is what gets sped up rather than kept or cut.

cut._backdrop_why: portrait phone clips fill a landscape canvas with a blurred, darkened copy of their own frame instead of black bars; ignored where the frame already covers 90% of the canvas
cut._blur_mode_why: a real blur, not a filled box and not a mosaic. Blur the sensitive field; never wipe a region.

_benign_why: store support numbers printed in every header/footer, empty-form placeholders, and the masked PAN the user cleared. track-blur.py reads this list.
_blur_kinds_why: review pass 1: 'I'm not against showing these balances' -- and blurring them in some frames but not others was the inconsistency complained about. Names and delivery branches are not in the list either: this OCR cannot read Cyrillic names, so claiming to cover them would be a promise the tool cannot keep. Review pass 2: 'email — no blur needed' (agamanuk@gmail.com is the user's own address).
